Mechanical keyboard for iphone

Illustration·by @LynelDesign·2026-08-24·inspora page·original post

What it is

Mechanical keyboard for iPhone (illustration): a 3D-rendered iOS-style soft keyboard - prediction bar ('The', the, to), white sculpted keycaps with deep rounding and soft shadows, blue return key, emoji/mic row; close-up shows glossy bezel curvature. Keys depress with a mechanical-style travel when tapped.

Build prompt

Rebuild these static renders 1:1, pixel-faithful: a mechanical keyboard for iPhone (illustration) - a 3D-rendered iOS-style soft keyboard with prediction bar ("The", the, to), white sculpted keycaps with deep rounding and soft shadows, a blue return key, emoji/mic row, and a macro close-up of the glossy bezel curvature.

## Stack
React + TypeScript + Tailwind (or SVG). This is a material-rendering exercise: layered shadows, top-light, ambient occlusion in the gaps. Static, with one optional micro-interaction.

## Scene
Render 1: full keyboard on a pale backdrop - 3 key rows + modifiers, prediction bar above, emoji and mic glyphs in the bottom tray; keycaps chunky with 8px radius, top-lit, soft AO in the gaps; blue return key glows slightly. Render 2: macro shot of the bottom-left corner - chrome-grey device bezel curve, emoji key, ABC/shift keys; glossy material, seam lines, cap legends.

## Motion spec
Optional key press only: keycap translateY 2px + inner shadow tightening, 80ms ease-in down, 120ms spring release. Nothing else moves.

## Calibration
- The 3D read comes from soft shadows under each cap + AO in the gaps, not from gradients on the cap faces.
- Top-light is consistent across every key; one light source.
- Prediction bar is flat and quiet - it must not compete with the sculpted keys.

## Reduced motion
N/A - static renders.

## Don't miss
- 8px cap radius and chunky proportions are the iOS-mechanical hybrid look; standard keyboard radius reads as neither.
- The blue return key is the only color accent and it glows slightly.
- Macro shot must show the bezel's glossy curvature and seam lines - the materials are the subject.
